name: Richard D. Fairbank

career.organization: Strategic Planning Associates (later Mercer Management Consulting)
career.title: Management consultant; ran the financial services practice
Co-founder and head of new credit card division (with Nigel Morris)

background_rationale: Co-founded the data-driven credit card business at Signet Bank that was spun off as Capital One in 1994 and has led it as CEO ever since, after seven years as a management consultant.

notable.summary: After Capital One disclosed a data breach affecting about 100 million people in the U.S. and 6 million in Canada, Fairbank said he sincerely apologized and was committed to making it right.
Completed the all-stock acquisition of Discover Financial, announced in February 2024 at about $35.3 billion, making Capital One the largest U.S. credit card issuer.
Agreed to acquire business-payments fintech Brex for $5.15 billion in stock and cash, saying the deal accelerates Capital One's push into business payments.
Capital One announced layoffs of more than 1,100 employees at the former Discover headquarters in Riverwoods, Illinois.

personal_story.hook: Fairbank and his co-founder pitched their data-driven credit card idea to about 20 banks before one said yes.
personal_story.summary: Fairbank is the son of two physicists; his father, William Fairbank, was a Stanford physics professor, and Fairbank has said he feels his father's presence and optimism every day. As a Stanford undergraduate he founded a swimming school because he wanted to work with children, and he ran a community recreation agency before returning to Stanford for an MBA in 1981. As a consultant at Strategic Planning Associates he noticed that banks sat on rich customer data but still sold one-size-fits-all credit cards. In 1988 he and Nigel Morris pitched an information-based alternative to about 20 banks before Signet Bank in Virginia let them run a new card division. He has described the next stretch as four years of near-death experiences before the first success; in 1994 Signet spun the business off as Capital One, with Fairbank as CEO.

quote.text: Don't take a job because it would look great on your resume. The resume that really matters is the one between your two ears.
